commits.author: ethantsliu
commits.message:
[levanter] Check accelerator before mesh validation (#8973)

Fail accelerator-required runs before mesh validation when JAX falls
back to CPU. A TPU worker that restarts without its accelerator now
reports the missing accelerator instead of a secondary mesh-shape error.
The platform-dependent default for requiring an accelerator is
unchanged.

Fixes #3433

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[grug] Add automatic DualPipeV MoE training (#8739)

Add model-specific pipeline training for Grug MoE with JaxPP
equation-level ZeroBubble and DualPipeV schedules. The pipeline variant
imports unchanged attention, normalization, dense MLP, and Hugging Face
config classes from `experiments/grug/moe/model.py`. Its MoE, block, and
transformer definitions remain local because pipeline staging changes
their call surfaces. Parameters and Adam state are initialized on their
owning stages, and DualPipeV maps two logical stages to each physical
rank without materializing the full training state. Both schedules use
the same MPMD state and autodiff path. The loop in
`experiments/grug/moe_pipeline/train.py` initializes fresh parameters
and synthetic data with AdamW at learning rate 1e-4, beta1 0.9, beta2
0.95, and weight decay 0.1; checkpoint save and restore are not
implemented.

The locked root `pipeline` extra replaces the standard GPU environment
with JaxPP and its CUDA dependencies. It requires NCCL 2.31.2 because
NCCL 2.30.7 hangs the grouped-transfer path on current JaxPP. Normal
Fray dispatch selects this environment explicitly; the obsolete
side-install path is removed.

The Snowball 67B-A2B DualPipeV batch-256, 32-microbatch configuration
reaches 603,327 tokens/s and 19.46% median analytic MFU on 64 H100s. A
matched DualPipeV run at batch 128 and 16 microbatches reaches 543,490
tokens/s and 17.53%. Each median covers ten post-warmup steps. Peak
memory is 59.153 GB/device for both, and loss differs by 4.0e-5 after 14
synthetic-data steps. Command buffers remain disabled for both
configurations because JAX 0.11.0 with JaxPP 0.11.0 can deadlock during
multi-communicator initialization and execution (#7655).

Adding the microbatch axis requires an explicit output sharding tree for
the transformed JaxPP step. [Echo incident
312](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/312) records the partition-spec mismatch
and resolution.

Part of #7024

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Initialize the step counter on the training mesh (#8911)

Initialize the train state's step counter with replicated sharding on
the active mesh. `_init_state` supplies the exemplar used for both fresh
training and checkpoint restoration, so a restored counter receives the
exemplar's sharding. Previously, `_init_state` produced the counter
under GSPMD sharding while `train_step` returned it under
`NamedSharding`. JIT cache keys include input shardings; at the hero
shape, this mismatch caused the second training step to compile another
executable. Every other state leaf already has matching sharding across
a step.

Each GpuExecutable owns a CollectiveMemoryCache, so each train-step
executable registers an NCCL symmetric window over the same
collective-memory arena at the same base address. NCCL 2.30.7 accepts
the duplicate after NCCL commit 52f6d00 removed deduplication from
symMemoryObtain; ncclDevrFindWindow then resolves an address to the last
window registered at that address. Measured at the hero shape (d6144, 48
layers, EP64, ragged all-to-all, one rack), the implicit step sharding
produced two train-step compilations and two 20,293,761,024-byte window
registrations per rank: 128 of each across 64 ranks. Explicit
initialization produced one compilation and one registration per rank,
or 64 of each. Eleven racks without explicit step sharding registered
1408 windows across 704 ranks. The per-leaf sharding diff across a step
reports no drift with explicit initialization.

Issue #8861 manifests as the first ragged train step after a
capacity-limited evaluation failing with `ncclGroupEnd(): invalid
argument`. That evaluator stays disabled for ragged runs under #8859;
running it between ragged train steps under this change has not been
tested. A 12-layer run registers one window despite the same sharding
mismatch, which is unexplained. The #8870 hang was observed with two
executables per rank on every attempt; whether one executable removes it
is not yet known.

Fixes #8861

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Generate searchable MCP tools from application APIs (#8943)

Expose checked-in Marina application APIs at the authenticated
Streamable HTTP
endpoint `/api/marina/mcp/`. An MCP client initially sees `find_tool`
and
`call_tool`. FastMCP's BM25 transform searches app-namespaced operations
such as
`evaldash_read_logs`, and its OpenAPI provider derives their schemas and
executes
calls against each mounted ASGI application.

Applications opt in per FastAPI operation with typed `x-marina` risk
metadata.
Unmarked routes are excluded. The `read`, `write`, `external_write`, and
`destructive` values map to standard MCP annotations and remain
available at
`_meta.marina.risk`. Echo registers 19 existing operations and EvalDash
registers
five reads. Existing HTTP paths, authentication, and the EvalDash
background
lifecycle remain unchanged.

FastMCP replaces the custom operation-schema builder and catalog
endpoint.
Marin's direct MCP requirement is `mcp>=2` with no upper bound; the lock
resolves
to 2.2.0, and the Iris babysitter uses the MCP 2 `MCPServer` API. Agent
UI, page
context, and agent execution remain outside this change.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Score verified agent timeouts (#8947)

Count an `AgentTimeoutError` as a valid Harbor evaluation sample when
the verifier produced a reward. Unverified timeouts and other exceptions
remain infrastructure attrition.

OT-TBLite rejected a 100-trial evaluation with 100 verifier results
because 30 trials ended in score-bearing agent timeouts. The new
regression test covers the aggregate score and completion gate.

Part of #8151

Co-authored-by: Benjamin Feuer <penfever@gmail.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[levanter] Stabilize recovery crash injection (#8965)

Use `SIGKILL` instead of `os.abort()` for the fake trainer's crash case.
It models fatal signal recovery without invoking CI core-dump handling,
which can keep the aborting child alive until the supervisor deadman
overrides its crash classification. Crash and sticky injectors get 30
seconds for CI scheduling delays; the deliberate hang retains its
3-second deadman deadline.

The crash test failed independently on `main` in Actions runs
[33964429305](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/33964429305)
and
[34032323471](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/34032323471).
An initial timeout-only fix reproduced the failure after 30 seconds in
[run
34267493371](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/34267493371),
where the aborting child survived SIGTERM and the supervisor killed it
with SIGKILL. The incident record is [Echo
364](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/364).

Fixes #8964

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[inference] Pass local model paths to vLLM (#8946)

Convert `file://` cache results to decoded filesystem paths before
starting vLLM. Transformers 5 treats file URIs as Hugging Face
repository IDs, so pinned Hugging Face evaluations failed after the
cache download and before endpoint registration.

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Cut recursive object listings and unread worker bookkeeping (#8952)

Four independent cleanups, each removing work that ran but was never
used.

Levanter checkpoint discovery globbed `<root>/*` to find step
directories. fsspec
implements glob via `find`, and object stores serve `find` with an
undelimited
prefix listing, so every discovery enumerated every object under the
root — all
tensorstore chunks of every saved step — and discarded everything below
the first
level. This runs at each job start (trainer resume,
`latest_checkpoint_path`,
temporary-checkpoint discovery), so a root holding a few dozen
large-model
checkpoints cost hundreds of paged list round trips.
`_discover_checkpoint_paths_single`
now issues one delimited `ls`, and `is_checkpoint_path` reuses it
instead of its
own `<root>/*/metadata.json` glob. Results are unchanged: old and new
output match
for local paths, `file://`, `memory://`, leaf checkpoint directories,
and missing
roots. `is_checkpoint_path` had no coverage, so this adds a test for the
predicate.

The datakit `normalize_to_parquet` entry point walked its input files
and then
issued one `StoragePath.size()` per file to pick a shard count. Each is
a separate
object-metadata round trip — the rigging filesystem factory sets a
zero-second
GCS/S3 listing expiry, so none were cached — and sources such as
common_corpus
have ~10k shards. `_discover_files` now walks with `detail=True` and
returns
`{path: size}`, taking sizes from the list responses it already issues,
matching
`processing/tokenize/_core.glob_with_sizes`.

`Autoscaler.get_vm` and `get_init_log` lost their last caller when the
controller's
`GetWorkerStatus` handler stopped reporting VM state in #6730. Below
them,
`WorkerRegistry.vm_info` / `init_log`, the `TrackedWorker.bootstrap_log`
copy taken
at every worker registration, and `RemoteWorkerHandle.bootstrap_log`
with its four
implementations were all unread, including a per-worker in-memory
accumulation of
every bootstrap output line. Bootstrap output still reaches the worker
log through
the existing per-line `logger.info`.
`GetWorkerStatusResponse.bootstrap_logs`
remains declared in the proto and is still never set, so `iris cluster
vm logs` and
the dashboard bootstrap-log panel stay empty as before; removing a CLI
command or
reserving proto fields is a separate wire decision.

In the Zephyr coordinator, `_InFlightEntry.attempt` was written on every
dispatch
and never read — stale-report rejection uses
`run.task_attempts[shard_idx]`, and the
attempt the worker echoes back travels on `PullTask`.
`_record_shard_failure` and
the finished/unknown-execution branch of `report_error` each open-coded
"zero the
worker's counter snapshot, keep its generation watermark"; both now call
`_clear_worker_inflight_counters`, which already documents that
invariant for
`report_result`.

---------

Co-authored-by: nightshift <nightshift@marin.local>
Co-authored-by: nightshift-agent <nightshift@marin.invalid>

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
[cleanup] Delete dead decode-loop profiling, eval module, config fields (#8957)

Three unrelated dead-code deletions in levanter, marin, and iris.

The inference decode loop in `levanter/inference/engine.py` carried
leftover
profiling scaffolding: a "fake submit" probe that ran `jax.tree.flatten`
over
`(gen_state, model, sampler)` on every decode iteration and discarded
the
result, so that the per-iteration log could report how long the flatten
took.
The same loop detokenized the full sequence of every finished slot on
every
drain to build a `logger.debug` message. Finished slots stay finished
until they
are released, so that ran repeatedly even with debug logging off; it is
now
guarded by `logger.isEnabledFor`. Both are host work in a loop that
tracks host
time as its bottleneck. Also removed: a commented-out per-token debug
printer, a
`hasattr(fins, "sum")` guard on what is always a numpy array, an
unbalanced
paren in the decode-iteration log string, and `_ingest_outputs`, whose
body was
a `None` check that `_extract_outputs` already performs plus a forward
call.

`marin/evaluation/save_logprobs.py` lost its only caller when #8831
retired the
`*_on_pod` fray submission pattern and removed
`run_save_logprobs_on_pod`. The
module has no draccus wrapper, no `__main__` block, and no entry-point
registration, so nothing could reach it. Its shared imports
`load_eval_model`
and `with_pack` keep other callers.

`CoreweaveSliceConfig.gpu_class` and `.infiniband` were added by the
pydantic
config migration in #6652 and have never been read. The CoreWeave
NodePool
manifest builder constructs `spec` from `instance_type` and scheduling
labels
only, so `infiniband: true` in `ci-coreweave-gpu-smoke.yaml` was
accepted and
ignored. `_Config` sets `extra="forbid"`, so dropping the field also
required
dropping that YAML key; all nine shipped `lib/iris/config/*.yaml` files
still
load through `load_config()`.

---------
